alignments.note: One lexeme rendered by the two words *how large*; headed on *large* as the meaning-bearing word under rule 17, though a head on *how* (its interrogative force) remains defensible.
Anarthrous dative noun: the supplied case preposition *with* stays with the noun under rules 21 and 23, discontinuous over the adjective's own words per rule 15.
Subject pronoun is the verb's helper under rules 7 and 9; head on the lexical verb.
Case preposition *unto* rides with the pronoun.
Displaced by the possessive adjective under rules 20 and 54: *mine own* belongs to ἐμῇ, so the article realizes nothing.
First-person possessive adjective takes the whole English possessive expression under rule 54.
The article being unrepresented, the case preposition *with* stays with the noun under rules 21 and 23.
